zh.title: 台灣虎航迎開航12週年推全航線促銷 九州機票提撥捐款應援熊本
zh.summary: 台灣虎航推出開航12週年全航線促銷；9月起購買九州機票每張捐贈50元
body: 台灣虎航宣布迎接開航12週年，自2026年9月1日至12日舉辦線上集章抽獎活動，並預計於9月16日推出全航線機票促銷，適用旅行期間為2026年9月16日至2027年3月27日。同時，業者將於9月1日至10月31日實施公益加碼，凡購買九州地區機票每張將捐出新台幣50元予熊本地震義援金專戶。
另一方面，星宇航空亦持續擴展日本航網，先前已宣布正式進軍高雄市場，規劃自2027年1月1日起開闢由高雄出發前往神戶及沖繩的2條日本定期航線。

en.title: Tigerair Taiwan Marks 12th Anniversary with Ticket Sales and Kumamoto Relief Donation
en.summary: Tigerair Taiwan launches 12th anniversary flight promotions and donates funds for Kyushu ticket purchases to Kumamoto relief.
body: Tigerair Taiwan has announced promotional events to commemorate its 12th anniversary. The carrier will host an online stamp-collection activity from September 1 to 12, 2026, followed by a network-wide ticket promotion launch on September 16 for travel between September 16, 2026, and March 27, 2027. Additionally, from September 1 to October 31, the airline will donate NT$50 per Kyushu-region ticket sold to Kumamoto Prefecture's earthquake relief fund.

Meanwhile, STARLUX Airlines is expanding its Japanese route network by entering the Kaohsiung market. The airline plans to launch two new routes from Kaohsiung to Kobe and Okinawa starting January 1, 2027.

zh.title: NTSB調查海軍陸戰隊一號無線電故障 FAA已重設DCA塔台天線
zh.summary: NTSB調查顯示視距涵蓋不足致通訊中斷；FAA重置天線解除DCA近距風險
body: 根據美國國家運輸安全委員會（NTSB）發布的初步調查報告，2026年8月4日，搭乘美國總統川普的「海軍陸戰隊一號」（Marine One）Sikorsky VH-3D直升機從起飛點離開時，與美國華盛頓特區羅納德·里根華盛頓國家機場（DCA）的空中交通管制員發生無線電通訊故障。由於通訊中斷，塔台未能收到預期的起飛前3分鐘通報，隨後與特快航空（Envoy Air）一架飛往佛羅里達州彭薩科拉國際機場（PNS）的巴西航空工業（Embraer）E170客機（航班號為 Envoy Flight 3742）發生近距離接近事件。
NTSB指出，事發當時為當地時間約14時34分，海軍陸戰隊一號從Ellipse起飛，而特快航空客機則正從DCA的1號跑道起飛。海軍陸戰隊一號機組曾兩度嘗試呼叫塔台，第一次未能成功傳達，第二次訊號呈現斷續且無法辨識，嘗試透過安那柯斯提亞-博林聯合基地進行轉播亦告失敗。因塔台未收到警告，管制員隨即核准特快航空班機起飛。直到海軍陸戰隊一號爬升至一定高度建立無線電聯繫時，特快航空客機已在空中。

根據美國聯邦航空管理局（FAA）估計，兩架航空器在DCA以北約2海浬處，水平距離最接近時約為0.82海浬，垂直距離約為700英尺。NTSB表示，由於兩機垂直間隔約700英尺，已超過500英尺的最低標準，因此仍維持在規定的隔離限制內。特快航空機組在爬升過程中收到空中交通碰撞防止系統（TCAS）的交通告警（Traffic Advisory），但系統並未發出防撞諮詢命令（Resolution Advisory），雙方飛行員在告警當下均未目視看到對方航空器。
FAA技術人員在事後調查中發現，無線電通訊障礙主因為原設備與起飛點之間的視距涵蓋不足。為解決此一安全隱患，FAA將無線電設備從鄰近住宅區移設至DCA管制塔台頂端。後續測試結果顯示，無線電通訊障礙已獲解決，未再出現通訊中斷情形。

en.title: NTSB examines Marine One radio failure at DCA as FAA moves antenna to tower top
en.summary: NTSB reports radio failure led to DCA close proximity; FAA relocated antenna to tower top.
body: According to a preliminary report by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), a radio communications failure occurred on August 4, 2026, between Marine One and air traffic controllers at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA). The presidential helicopter, a Sikorsky VH-3D carrying US President Donald Trump, departed the Ellipse at approximately 14:34 local time when inadequate line-of-sight coverage prevented the crew's required departure notification from reaching the control tower.

At the same time, air traffic controllers at DCA cleared Envoy Air Flight 3742, an Embraer E170 bound for Pensacola International Airport (PNS) in Florida, for takeoff from Runway 1. Marine One crew members made two direct attempts to establish contact with the tower and tried to relay the warning through Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling, but the transmissions were either not received or broken. Radio contact was only established after the helicopter climbed to a higher altitude, by which time the regional jet was already airborne.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) estimated that the two aircraft came within approximately 0.82 nautical miles laterally and 700 feet vertically of each other about two miles north of DCA. The NTSB noted that the aircraft remained within required separation limits because their 700-foot vertical separation exceeded the 500-foot minimum threshold. Pilots of the Envoy jet received a Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) traffic advisory, though no resolution advisory directing evasive action was issued.

Following the encounter, FAA technicians determined that inadequate line-of-sight radio coverage from the former equipment location in a residential neighborhood caused the failure. The agency relocated the radio equipment to the top of the DCA control tower, and subsequent flight testing confirmed that the communications issue was fully resolved.
